clue.text: Short poem to cover a rod we hear

indicators.note: the phrase signals that the words before it are spoken and the entry is a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to cover is to deck, and a rod is a stick, so the phrase is 'deck a stick'

explanation.surface: Someone describes a brief verse whose subject is sheathing a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns 'deck a stick' (to cover a rod) into the poetic term that sounds like it.
explanation.definitionFit: A decastich is a ten-line verse, a short poem by line count.

clue.text: Under the affluence of incohol as Spooner would have put it

definitions.text: Under the affluence of incohol as Spooner would have put it

parts.words: Under the affluence of incohol as Spooner would have put it
parts.note: swap the starts back and the phrase is 'under the influence of alcohol', the state of someone intoxicated

explanation.surface: A tipsy speaker mangles a phrase in the manner of the Reverend Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue itself is a Spoonerism: 'affluence of incohol' is 'influence of alcohol' with sounds swapped, and the slurred delivery suits the condition it describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being under the influence of alcohol means being intoxicated, inebriated after too much to drink.

clue.text: Magpie caught Alice's mad associate with Her Majesty

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the Mad Hatter is a companion of Alice in Lewis Carroll's Wonderland
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A bird snatches a Wonderland character in the Queen's company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magpie' is used figuratively: a person who talks incessantly.
explanation.definitionFit: A magpie, figuratively, is a person who chatters without stopping, a babbler.

clue.text: Pinch a drop of sealing-wax as an amorous gesture

parts.note: to pinch is to steal
a kiss is an old word for a small drop of sealing-wax

explanation.surface: Someone filches a blob of wax from a letter, presented as something romantic.
explanation.walkthrough: KISS for a small drop of sealing-wax is a dictionary sense few solvers know.
explanation.definitionFit: Snatching a quick unexpected peck is a classic romantic act.

clue.text: Person within an organisation imprisoned ringleader

parts.note: someone imprisoned is inside, in slang
the leader, or first letter, of the word ring is R

explanation.surface: A member of a group has locked up the chief troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringleader' is read as 'ring leader', the first letter of 'ring'.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider is a member of a group with access to its private information.

clue.text: Grape used to make German port?

definitions.meaning: Black ... is a variety of dessert grape
the great port city on the Elbe in northern Germany

explanation.surface: A fruit is said to be the basis of a German fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the fortified wine, which grapes do make; it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: The grape variety and the north German harbour city share one name.

clue.text: Fastener left in military station

indicators.note: the letter for left is placed inside the word for a base

parts.note: a camp is a military station

explanation.surface: A clip has been abandoned at an army base.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamp is a device that grips things together, a kind of fastening tool.

clue.text: Tom Bowling was their darling

parts.note: Dibdin's sea song 'Tom Bowling' calls the dead sailor 'the darling of our' ship's company

explanation.surface: A beloved figure is remembered by a group of admirers.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Dibdin's 18th-century song 'Tom Bowling' mourns a sailor, 'the darling of our crew'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ship's company are those who sail together, and the song says Tom was their favourite.

clue.text: Is in drink in part of church

indicators.note: the word is goes inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink, a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Someone is in their cups inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage between the pews, a section of a church building.

clue.text: Store of crisp producers defined in 6 Across

definitions.text: Store of crisp producers defined in 6 Across

parts.words: Store of crisp producers defined in 6 Across
parts.note: crisps are made from tubers, and a heap of them stored under earth and straw is the farming sense of the word at 6 Across, CLAMP

explanation.surface: A warehouse for snack manufacturers is described in another entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crisp producers' are the vegetables crisps are made from, not factories; 6 Across, CLAMP, also means such a storage heap.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamp or pit is a mound of root vegetables stored under soil for winter, the spuds that become crisps.

clue.text: Practice that makes us get older

parts.note: to get older is to age

explanation.surface: A habit that causes us to grow old.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is customary practice, the way something is habitually done.

clue.text: Cartwheel going sideways in season to plant

parts.note: summer is a season
to set seeds is to plant them

explanation.surface: A gymnast's sideways roll is performed at planting time.
explanation.walkthrough: SUMMERSET is an old spelling of somersault; the clue's 'Cartwheel going sideways' stretches it to a sideways roll.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic form of somersault, an acrobatic tumble, here a sideways one.

clue.text: Boiler with cylindrical container for a large tea-party

parts.note: a kettle boils water
a drum is a cylindrical container

explanation.surface: Kitchen equipment is assembled for a big tea gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an old sense: an 18th-century large and lively afternoon party was called a kettledrum.
explanation.definitionFit: In the 18th and 19th centuries a big informal afternoon social gathering was nicknamed this.

clue.text: Hide from shower

definitions.meaning: an animal's skin, as a noun
to shower with missiles or to rain hard

explanation.surface: Someone takes cover from a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' reads as a verb, to take cover; it is the noun, an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelt is an animal skin; to pelt is to bombard or pour down.

clue.text: Fly! It could be a policeman!

definitions.meaning: a large buzzing blowfly
old slang for a police officer, from the blue uniform

explanation.surface: Someone yells 'Run!' on seeing an officer approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly!' reads as a command to flee; it is the insect. The police sense is dated British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The bluebottle is a blowfly; the word was also nineteenth-century slang for a constable in blue.

clue.text: One who plays in diamonds is not working

definitions.meaning: a batter on a baseball diamond strikes at the ball
someone who has downed tools in a dispute

explanation.surface: A card player holding diamonds is idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diamonds' suggests a card suit; it is the baseball field.
explanation.definitionFit: A striker hits the ball in a ball game, and also refuses to work in an industrial dispute.

clue.text: University petition to make up plastic

indicators.note: the letters are used to make a new word, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A student asks a college to manufacture synthetic material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' rearranges the letters of UP PLASTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: At Cambridge a supplicat is a formal petition, for instance for a degree.

clue.text: Wild flower in gold-coloured vessel

parts.note: gilt means coated or coloured with gold
a cup is a drinking vessel

explanation.surface: A meadow bloom has been placed in a golden goblet.
explanation.definitionFit: Giltcup is a country name for the buttercup, a wild flower of fields.

clue.text: Box with paper money in the lowest register

parts.note: a chest is a box
a note is a piece of paper money

explanation.surface: A strongbox stuffed with banknotes is kept at the bottom of the ledger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'register' suggests a ledger or till; it is the vocal range.
explanation.definitionFit: Chest notes are sung in the lowest vocal range, resonating in the chest.

clue.text: Turkish coin and note — en tout cas

parts.note: the para is a small Turkish coin
sol is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Coins and a banknote are tucked into a French umbrella.
explanation.walkthrough: 'en tout cas' (French, 'in any case') is a combined sunshade and umbrella.
explanation.definitionFit: An en-tout-cas is a sunshade usable as an umbrella, so a type of sunshade.

clue.text: Seek and select a watch

definitions.meaning: to search for and pick out, as in finding a suitable item
a guard keeping vigil, or the post they keep

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for a wristwatch and picks one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch' suggests a timepiece; it is a sentry.
explanation.definitionFit: To look out something is to find and choose it; a lookout is a sentinel keeping watch.

clue.text: Exhibit gift now

definitions.meaning: to show or display, a verb
a gift given to someone
the current time

explanation.surface: A display of something given right now.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: to show, a gift, and the time that is current.

clue.text: Muffin in the American way with cancelled service

parts.note: a pike, short for turnpike, is an American toll road
in tennis a let is a serve that is replayed

explanation.surface: A breakfast bun is served the American way with breakfast cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests waiting at table; it is a tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: A pikelet is a small thick pancake, a type of crumpet or muffin.

clue.text: Be pleased with the same thing

definitions.meaning: to enjoy or approve of
as in 'the ...', an equal or counterpart

explanation.surface: Someone is happy to have an identical item.
explanation.definitionFit: To like is to enjoy; 'the like' means something equal or similar.

clue.text: A pool for Jack?

definitions.meaning: a shared fund of money
in the game of bowls the small target ball

explanation.surface: Someone asks if there's a swimming pool for a man called Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a name; it is the target ball in lawn bowls, also called the kitty.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty is a pooled fund; it is also another name for the jack in bowls.

clue.text: The lowest possible action of a belly-dancer

definitions.meaning: the absolute minimum level
the dancer sways and shakes the hips and rear

explanation.surface: A belly-dancer's movements are judged the worst there are.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: a dancer's motion is to rock the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock bottom is the lowest level; a dancer's swaying hips also rock the backside.

clue.text: Measured me spread out for drying

parts.note: to ted hay is to turn and spread it to dry

explanation.surface: Someone was laid out to dry and measured.
explanation.definitionFit: Meted means allotted or measured out.

clue.text: Shoot a child

definitions.meaning: a sprout on a potato or seed
a young child or a pert girl

explanation.surface: Someone is told to fire at a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' reads as a verb to fire; it is a plant sprout.
explanation.definitionFit: A chit is a young sprout and, dismissively, a young girl.

clue.text: Constable required to apprehend parrot

parts.note: to apprehend is to catch
Poll is a traditional name for a pet parrot

explanation.surface: A policeman is needed to arrest a parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchpoll was a sheriff's officer, a petty constable or bailiff.

clue.text: Schubert's quintet of interest to Izaak Walton

definitions.meaning: Schubert's Piano Quintet in A is named after a fish
Walton wrote The Compleat Angler, about fishing

explanation.surface: A piece of chamber music appeals to a famous seventeenth-century writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Izaak Walton was the 17th-century author of The Compleat Angler, the classic book on fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Schubert's quintet bears this fish's name, and an angler hunts the same fish.

clue.text: Agree to meet in a cattle-fair

definitions.meaning: an old verb sense, to arrange a meeting
a Scottish word for a livestock market

explanation.surface: Two people arrange a rendezvous at a livestock market.
explanation.walkthrough: The cattle-fair sense is Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is an arranged meeting, and in Scotland also a market for cattle.

clue.text: Rank action needed for proof of possession

parts.note: a title is a rank, as of a noble
a deed is an action

explanation.surface: A rank-and-file action is needed to prove ownership.
explanation.definitionFit: A title deed is the legal document proving ownership of property.
